content: 1. Both fluphenazine and fluconazole are known to prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, or alternative medications should be considered. 2. Fluconazole and formoterol also increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 3. The combination of gilteritinib and fluconazole significantly increases the QTc interval and is contraindicated. 4. Fluconazole and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concurrent use, and as clinically indicated. Discontinue treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 5. Fluconazole and glasdegib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor for an increased risk of QTc prolongation. 6. Haloperidol and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative medications. 7. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Fluconazole increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 9. Fluconazole increases the levels of imipramine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 10. Fluconazole increases the levels of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 11. Fluconazole and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor electrolytes before and after initiation of any QTc-prolonging drug, and periodically during treatment. 12. Isoflurane and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. Fluconazole and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 14. Fluconazole increases the levels of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid combining ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Ivosidenib and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. If coadministration of QTc-prolonging drugs is unavoidable, monitor for an increased risk of QTc prolongation. 16. Fluconazole and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 17. Lefamulin and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 18. Fluconazole increases the levels of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid combining lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 19. Fluconazole and levoketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 20. Lofepramine and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Fluconazole increases the levels of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Fluconazole and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 23. Fluconazole increases the levels of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 24. Macimorelin and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. Macimorelin increases the QTc interval by approximately 11 ms. Avoid coadministration with QTc-prolonging drugs to reduce the risk of torsades de pointes. Allow sufficient washout time of QTc-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 25. Maprotiline and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 26. Fluconazole increases the levels of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Combining moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam increases systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 27. Mirtazapine and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 28. Fluconazole and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 29. Fluconazole increases the levels of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 30. Fluconazole increases the levels of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid combining neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 31. Fluconazole and nilotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 32. Fluconazole increases the levels of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 33. Nortriptyline and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 34. Fluconazole and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 35. Fluconazole increases the levels of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 36. Fluconazole increases the levels of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects occur, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 37. Fluconazole and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. Avoid in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended with concomitant QTc-prolonging medications, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 38. Oxaliplatin and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 39. Fluconazole increases the levels of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 40. Fluconazole and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. Panobinostat significantly prolongs the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against combining it with QTc-prolonging drugs. 41. Fluconazole increases the levels of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 42. Fluconazole increases the levels of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 43. Perphenazine and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 44. Fluconazole increases the levels of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. 45. Fluconazole and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 46. Prochlorperazine and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 47. Promazine and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 48. Promethazine and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 49. Protriptyline and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 50. Fluconazole increases the levels of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 51. Fluconazole increases the levels of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 52. Fluconazole decreases the effects of Saccharomyces boulardii through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. Systemic or oral antifungals may reduce the activity of probiotics. 53. Fluconazole increases the levels of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. 54. Sevoflurane and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 55. Fluconazole increases the levels of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 56. Fluconazole increases the levels of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 57. Fluconazole increases the levels of siponimod by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Combining siponimod with moderate CYP2C9 and moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. 58. Siponimod and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 59. Fluconazole increases the levels of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 60. Fluconazole and sotalol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 61. Fluconazole increases the levels of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per the drug monograph. 62. Tetrabenazine and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 63. Thioridazine and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 64. Fluconazole increases the levels of tofacitinib by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg/day when combined with moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 65. Fluconazole increases the levels of tolvatpan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 66. Trazodone and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 67. Trifluoperazine and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 68. Trimipramine and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 69. Fluconazole increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. Exercise extreme caution when combining vilanterol with QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 70. Fluconazole and vandetanib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 71. Vemurafenib and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 72. Fluconazole increases the levels of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 73. Fluconazole increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. Exercise extreme caution when combining vilanterol with QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 74. Fluconazole increases the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If intolerable adverse effects occur, reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 75. Fluconazole and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combination or use alternative therapies. 76. Fluconazole increases the levels of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if combined with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 77. Albuterol and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 78. Fluconazole increases the levels of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. Fluconazole increases the levels of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Fluconazole increases the levels of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Fluconazole increases the levels of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 82. Apomorphine and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 83. Fluconazole increases the levels of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 84. Arformoterol and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely.
